heroText: Rovaniemi is Lapland's Arctic Circle capital, built around winter travel, river landscapes and Santa Claus Village. Start at Santa Claus Village, visit Arktikum for northern history, then use Ounasvaara or Kemijoki riverside for outdoor time. Rovaniemi Airport is close, but winter arrivals need realistic transfer and clothing plans.

areas.name: Rovaniemi centre
areas.text: The centre is best for restaurants, shopping, tour pickups, the station and easy riverside walks.

areas.name: Santa Claus Village
areas.text: Santa Claus Village is best for family-focused stays, Arctic Circle photos and early access to themed attractions.

areas.name: Ounasvaara
areas.text: Ounasvaara suits outdoor stays with forest trails, winter sports and quieter hotels above the centre.

areas.name: Korkalovaara
areas.text: Korkalovaara is a residential area useful for apartments, longer stays and travellers with a car.

airports.name: Rovaniemi Airport (RVN)
airports.text: Rovaniemi Airport is north of the centre near Santa Claus Village, with taxis, buses and hotel transfers.

airportTransfer.value: 10-20 min by taxi or transfer to Santa Claus Village or the centre
airportTransfer.distance: about 8 km north of central Rovaniemi

stayOverview: Stay in Rovaniemi centre for restaurants and tour pickups, Santa Claus Village for family Christmas travel, Ounasvaara for nature and winter sports, or Korkalovaara for apartments and car-based stays.
hotelIntro: Rovaniemi is very seasonal. Centre hotels are most practical, Santa Claus Village is themed and family-focused, Ounasvaara is calmer and outdoorsy, and apartments work well when tours include pickups.
rentalCars: A car helps for cabins and independent aurora chasing, but many winter tours include transfers from central hotels.

history.text: Periodic clearance of new land for agriculture and the practice of slash-and-burn cultivation began around 750–530 BC.

Rovaniemi is first mentioned by name in official documents in 1453, existing as a set of small villages whose inhabitants earned their living mainly in agriculture and animal husbandry—with fishing and hunting the most.

history.label: 1800s
